transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Ellen Park, Miguel Torres, Aisha Patel, Samir Desai, Priya Reddy
---
[00:00] Ellen: Okay, uh, thanks everyone for joining on time. I'll kick off real quick. This is our monthly IT / Finance / Security admin sync — main goals today are SOC 2 prep status, RBAC alignment, KMS key rotation, and billing allocations for the Dedicated pools.
[00:20] Miguel: Hi all, sorry bit late, at my desk now.
[00:25] Samir: Morning — or afternoon — depending on your timezone.
[00:30] Aisha: Good to be here.
[00:32] Priya: Hi team.
[00:35] Ellen: Cool. Quick round-robin updates. Aisha, security first — how's the SOC 2 evidence collection?
[00:45] Aisha: Uh, we're about 65% there. We have HR and onboarding docs, policies, change management artifacts. Still missing: proof of RBAC enforcement for service accounts across the Dedicated clusters, and a clear KMS rotation schedule for customer-managed keys. Also need confirmation on log retention windows from finance for billing reasons.
[01:05] Priya: For the RBAC piece, I reviewed the last matrix, it's kinda stale. There are orphaned roles on the dev Dedicated pools, and some service accounts are in the wrong groups. I can propose a cleanup but need owners to sign off.
[01:20] Ellen: Yup we should do an owners review. I'll share an updated RBAC matrix by Tuesday. That'll include app owner contact info.
[01:27] Miguel: On KMS rotation — we have a plan for the control plane keys, but the customer-managed KMS (for Private) rotations haven't been documented end-to-end. I'll run a dry-run in staging next week and capture the runbook steps. There was also that weird issue where the rotation didn't reattach a couple of HSM policies in staging — I need to investigate.
[01:50] Aisha: Please capture that, Miguel; the auditor will want a reproducible runbook.
[01:55] Samir: Quick finance note — we've seen a ~12% month-over-month increase in Dedicated spend in July, mainly from two high-throughput customers and one internal POC. I want to propose a cost-allocation model where we tag by team and route charges accordingly — that will help show up in the audit too.
[02:15] Priya: Sounds good. Would that tagging affect RBAC or is it separate?
[02:20] Samir: Mostly separate, it's billing tags. But we need engineering to adopt the tags on deployment pipelines.
[02:26] Miguel: We can add tags in infra templates, but need a small change in CI/CD to propagate them. Not hard but we need a rollout plan so we don't break existing stacks.
[02:40] Ellen: Okay, action item for Miguel to coordinate with the platform teams.
[02:45] 
[05:00] Aisha: Another item — audit log retention. Right now, control-plane logs are retained 90 days in Splunk by default; some teams want 365 for compliance reasons. We need to estimate the cost delta if we bump to 365 for specific indices.
[05:20] Samir: I'll model that. Can you give me the current ingestion rates for the control plane vs Dedicated customer log sets?
[05:27] Aisha: Yes, I'll pull last 90 days and share; plus any PII-hits we've redacted.
[05:35] Miguel: Note, the ingestion spikes correlate with our nightly KV cache backups and some large model-load events — may be noise, but worth normalizing when you run the numbers.
[06:00] Priya: On pen test — we have vendor proposals from two shops. One is more expensive but has more red-team capabilities. We should scope the test to include Private deployments (on-prem) and the VPC connector flows.
[06:15] Ellen: Agreed. Priya, can you finalize the scope and send to procurement?
[06:20] Priya: Yep, target to finalize by 8/21.
[06:25] 
[10:12] Samir: Back to Dedicated capacity — engineering asked if we can justify reserved capacity vs burst for Q4. Finance would like a recommendation because the commit terms affect how we book revenue and forecast.
[10:30] Miguel: From infra's perspective, reserved capacity gives predictable scheduling and lower per-token cost, but it's risky if utilization drops. We can recommend a mixed approach — reserve base capacity and allow burst pools. Also quantify ROI given historical utilization.
[10:50] Samir: If we forecast wrong, finance will have to mark down unused commit, which impacts the quarter. So we need 1) a utilization baseline, 2) a sensitivity analysis. I'll run scenario models if you provide utilization numbers.
[11:05] Miguel: I'll export the historical utilization for the Dedicated pools and tag by customer and internal usage.
[11:10] 
[15:00] Aisha: One operational gotcha — our KV cache eviction logs were mildly corrupted in the July incident; there's transcription of the error as "KV cash" in the postmortem notes (ha), but we should double-check the event correlation. It may have caused duplicate billing of short-lived ops.
[15:20] Miguel: I recall that. There was a race condition during concurrent scale-down. Fix is in the branch, but we need a backport for a couple prod clusters.
[15:30] Ellen: Please prioritize a safe backport. Put me in the PR review thread.
[15:35] Miguel: Will do.
[20:00] Priya: Compliance Q — do we have an answer for data residency controls requested by a European customer? They asked if we can pin models to EU-hosted Dedicated pools and ensure KMS keys never leave region.
[20:20] Miguel: Yes, we support region-scoped Dedicated, but we need to formally document the routing guarantees and the KMS regional constraints. It's in our private deployment docs but not in the public security pack.
[20:35] Aisha: Let's add a section to the security packet that explicitly lists regional deployment guarantees and KMS rules. That will help SOC 2 and procurement requests.
[20:45] Ellen: Who will take that? Aisha?
[20:48] Aisha: I can draft it, but I'll need help from Miguel for the infra wording.
[20:55] 
[25:00] Samir: On invoicing — small ask: can we get better line-level usage export for billing exports? The current CSV lumps some charges and isn't easy to ingest into our accounting system.
[25:15] Miguel: We can extend the export, but need to coordinate with the billing service owner. I can start a ticket and include the schema change.
[25:25] Samir: Thanks. If you can target a prototype export by 8/20, I can test it with finance systems.
[25:32] 
[30:00] Ellen: Okay, let's recap owners: RBAC matrix — Ellen; Audit logs extraction — Aisha; Billing allocation and forecast modeling — Samir; KMS rotation doc + dry-run — Miguel; Pen test scope — Priya. Dates aligned with action items.
[30:15] Priya: Quick question about SSO/SAML audit artifacts — we need proof of SSO enforcement for third-party contractors. Do we have a current export?
[30:30] Aisha: We can pull SAML login events but need to map contractors by group. I think HR needs to confirm contractor list.
[30:40] Ellen: I'll loop in People Ops.
[35:00] Miguel: Minor note — we should tag internal POC projects so finance doesn't over-allocate costs to customers. Some internal experiments are using Dedicated pools without proper tags. I'll add a guard in the deploy pipeline to require a cost center tag.
[35:20] Samir: That will help.
[35:25] Aisha: Also, when we run the pen test, we should consider a scoped run against the private control plane, not just the tenant surfaces.
[35:35] Priya: Agreed.
[40:00] Ellen: Any other blockers?
[40:05] Samir: None from finance other than data for modeling.
[40:10] Miguel: No blockers, will prioritize backport.
[40:12] Aisha: No blockers; will share logs.
[40:15] Priya: I'll start vendor outreach.
[40:20] Ellen: Great. Let's set follow-up for 2026-08-25 same time. I'll send calendar invite and action item tracker.
[40:30] 
[45:00] Ellen: Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.
---
Notes: transcript contains occasional ASR errors (speaker labels merged, short mis-hearings like "KV cash" vs "KV cache"). References to documentation and decks: "security-packet-v2.pdf" (shared in chat), RBAC spreadsheet (link omitted), billing export sample (attachement).
